note: Append-only activity log. The verification pipeline writes an entry for every field-level change it makes; humans write entries for decisions. This is what the /updates page renders, and it is the audit trail that makes an autonomous board trustworthy.

kinds.changed: A tracked field changed on an existing entry
kinds.verified: Confidence moved up — a claim got corroborated or confirmed
kinds.missed: A deadline passed without us acting

updates.title: Mintek-SCi Grad Hackathon 2026 — application submitted
updates.body: Team applied in time. Status moved to applied, awaiting Mintek's response.

updates.title: Discovery Gradhack 2026 — correction: Team Sonar competed, placed Top 6
updates.body: The 2026-08-10 entry below recorded this as missed. That was wrong — the team made the deadline and competed, placing Top 6. Discovery of the event was still late (only signal beforehand was an empty team calendar), which is a real gap worth fixing, but the outcome was a result, not a miss. Corrected in data/opportunities.json.

updates.title: Board widened from hackathons to opportunities
updates.body: Added a `kind` field so the board covers competitions, graduate programmes, recruiting events and accelerators — not just hackathons. Two entries were reclassified on migration: BCG Platinion is a `recruiting_event` (the event is the interview) and Mintek-SCi is a `grad_programme`. Also added `career_track` to mark the three entries that are direct hiring routes.

updates.title: Discovery Gradhack 2026 — missed by three days
updates.body: Ran 7 August 2026 at Discovery Place, Sandton. 50 IT students from SA universities, teams of 2–4, free entry, R12 500 per winning team member, plus a permanent-employment pathway. It was the board's #1 open action item and the only signal was an empty team calendar. Moved to past. Predicted-window watch set for ~August 2027.

updates.title: ADTC prize conflict closed — arithmetic confirms the earlier ruling
updates.body: Press reported "$20,000+" against Devpost's itemised $16,500. Confirmed by arithmetic that both are correct and describe different things: 8000+4000+3000+1500 = $16,500 cash, and 10×$250 + 20×$50 = $3,500 in GPU credits, totalling exactly $20,000. No action needed.

updates.title: ADTC — possible second stage, unresolved
updates.body: Sources still report 25 August against the board's 24 August, and one describes it as a "first-stage deadline" for "initial proposals". The board models this as a single submit-once deadline. Keeping Devpost's earlier date — submitting early is free — but flagged for a manual check of the organiser page before the 24th.

updates.title: Initial board — 17 entries, calendar, playbook, CLI
updates.body: First full research pass. Every date carries a source link and a confidence level; conflicts recorded with the reasoning behind each ruling.
